claims.explanation: U-18666A is a known inhibitor of oxidosqualene cyclase and also disrupts intracellular cholesterol transport, causing lysosomal cholesterol accumulation. Selectivity may arise from cancer cells with high cholesterol demand or altered cholesterol trafficking, particularly those with PTEN loss or PI3K pathway activation, which can increase cholesterol synthesis and uptake. Additionally, squamous lineage and certain driver mutations may sensitize to cholesterol transport disruption.

features.basis: PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, increasing cholesterol synthesis and dependence; observed in multiple sensitive lines (ZR751, 786O, UACC62, HEC265).
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K signaling, potentially increasing cholesterol demand; seen in sensitive lines (KYSE510, SNU840).
KRAS mutations may alter lipid metabolism and increase dependence on cholesterol; observed in sensitive lines (KPNSI9S, GSU, SNU410).
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines, but also in resistant lines; may reflect general genomic instability.
BRAF mutations in sensitive melanoma lines (K029AX, UACC62) may link to altered lipid metabolism.
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK, potentially affecting cholesterol homeostasis; seen in sensitive lines (BICR6, S117).
EGFR mutations in sensitive lung lines (NCIH1650) may increase cholesterol uptake; however, resistant lines also have EGFR mutations.
CDKN2A loss in sensitive lines (SNU1214, K029AX) may alter cell cycle and lipid metabolism.
KMT2D mutations appear more frequent in resistant lines (KYSE270, SNUC5, FTC133), suggesting a protective role.
FBXW7 mutations are common in resistant lines (CL11, MKN1, SNUC5, NCIH1648), possibly indicating reduced sensitivity.
ARID1A mutations appear in several resistant lines (KU1919, SNUC5, LOXIMVI), suggesting protection.
ATM mutations in resistant lines (SNUC5, SNU685) may indicate a protective effect.
